ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Eva Perón — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Review three months after treatment: PET-CT response, examination, anemia, mood, and the follow-up plan

text.paragraph: Review three months after treatment, with the PET-CT result. [S]

Ms. Perón returns three and a half months after finishing treatment. Her PET-CT a week ago showed a complete metabolic response, with no uptake in the cervix, nodes or elsewhere, and Dr. Osei-Bonsu's examination last month found no tumor. The estradiol patch and progesterone stopped the hot flashes and night sweats within a few weeks. She uses the dilator three times a week; intercourse is comfortable with a lubricant. Her energy is nearly back, she has regained weight, and she is working full days again. She has had no bleeding, pelvic or back pain, or leg swelling. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1951-08-17; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Cervix small, pale and smooth, with radiation changes and no mass; upper vagina mildly narrowed; rectovaginal examination: parametria soft, without nodularity

Bleeding after intercourse and between periods, with heavier periods, for about four months, with tiredness and a dull pelvic ache. Never had cervical screening. Speculum examination shows a friable, exophytic mass about 4 cm across on the cervix that bleeds on contact. Punch biopsy, HPV test and cytology taken; urgent gynecologic oncology consultation booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem linked to her documented abnormal bleeding with anemia; superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 72 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs
S — Synthetic modern finding linked to her documented anemia from vaginal bleeding.

Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, HPV 16 positive: an exophytic tumor about 4.5 cm across with clinical involvement of the left parametrium, not reaching the pelvic wall; pelvic MRI and PET-CT ordered for FIGO 1943 staging. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented cervical cancer
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

Acute cystitis during pelvic chemoradiation: two days of new burning, urgency and cloudy urine on top of mild radiation frequency, without fever or flank pain; urine dipstick positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrite; culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; neutrophil count and kidney function normal; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.
Ovarian failure after pelvic radiation, with hot flashes, night sweats, poor sleep and vaginal dryness two weeks after treatment; FSH 72 mIU/mL and estradiol 14 pg/mL
S — Synthetic expected effect of pelvic chemoradiation.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, FIGO 1943 stage IIB (C53.9). No evidence of disease: complete metabolic response on PET-CT and no tumor on examination. A written survivorship care plan, in Spanish, was given: gynecologic oncology review every three months for two years, then every six months; no routine imaging unless symptoms arise; warning symptoms to report. [S]
Gynecologic oncology review next month.
Continue the dilator.
Report vaginal bleeding, pelvic or back pain, leg swelling, or weight loss without waiting.

Ovarian failure after pelvic radiation (E89.41). Symptoms controlled; blood pressure normal; no clot symptoms. [S]
Continue estradiol and progesterone.

Iron deficiency anemia (D50.0). Resolved: hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL and ferritin 48 ng/mL now that the bleeding has stopped. [S]
Stop ferrous sulfate.
